title: Connection governance at scale with connection recency
summary: Use the connection-recency signals (createdDateTime, lastBoundDateTime, lastCredentialUsedDateTime) exposed by 'connection list' plus the derived 'connection find-stale / find-duplicates / find-single-owner' commands to find and safely retire stale/duplicate connections and fix single-owner orphan risk. Gateways cap at 1,000 connections, so hygiene keeps you under the limit.
why_it_matters: Connections are shared infrastructure — pipelines, dataflows, semantic models, and notebooks reference them so credentials are not stored per item. Across a large tenant they grow exponentially: inconsistent names, departed owners, and multiple connections pointing at the same endpoint. On-premises/VNet gateways have a hard limit of 1,000 connections, so uncontrolled sprawl eventually blocks new connections. Recency data gives the signals to review and retire safely.

signals.createdDateTime: When the connection was created. Used to gate assessment: connections created before connection-recency GA (~March 2026) report NULL recency even when actively used.
signals.lastBoundDateTime: When an item was most recently linked. NULL on a post-GA connection means no event was reported, a review signal rather than authoritative coverage of ALL current dependencies.
signals.lastCredentialUsedDateTime: When the credentials were most recently used by any workload. Can lag real time by up to ~30 minutes, so use it for governance/investigation, not live monitoring.
signals.myLastBoundDateTime / myLastCredentialUs: The same two signals scoped to the calling user only.

commands.fabio connection find-stale: Flags never-bound / never-used / credentials-unused connections. Defaults: --unused-days 90, --created-after 2026-05-01 (the safe post-GA cutoff). READ-ONLY.
commands.fabio connection find-duplicates: Groups connections with similar target metadata (type + path + connectivity type + gateway) and suggests a most-recently-used keepId heuristic. It does not establish interchangeable credentials or which one is safe to retire. Add --match-credential-type to distinguish credential types. READ-ONLY.
commands.fabio connection find-single-owner: Flags connections whose ONLY Owner is an individual User (orphan risk when they leave). READ-ONLY.

safe_workflow: REVIEW, don't auto-delete: recency is the starting point, not a delete trigger. Some connections are legitimately seasonal (year-end/holiday runs) — widen --unused-days or spot-check before acting.

Retirement preview only after full dependency/owner review: fabio --wrap-untrusted --readonly connection delete --id <ID> --dry-run. Do not pipe candidate IDs directly into mutations. Explicit human approval is required before applying a separate destructive operation.

Treat find-duplicates keepId as a heuristic, not a chosen winner. Review all consumers, security settings, authentication and permissions before any separately approved rebinding/consolidation; target similarity never authorizes deletion.

Review continuity with a separately selected durable group, not a guessed principal. A guarded preview is fabio --wrap-untrusted --readonly connection add-role-assignment --id <ID> --principal-id <GROUP> --principal-type Group --role Owner --dry-run. Group ownership is not proof of membership, source grants or credential handoff; do not apply changes automatically.
gotchas: For bounded tenant-admin evidence and review plans, use admin connection-hygiene with explicit --id values or an opt-in --inventory scan. It distinguishes missing/malformed/partial evidence from absence, never chooses a duplicate winner, and never applies cleanup/grants. See admin-connection-hygiene.

find-stale excludes malformed timestamps instead of interpreting a parse failure as never-bound/never-used. Legacy labels and find-duplicates keepId remain review heuristics, not deletion eligibility, credential equivalence or complete dependency coverage.
Linking != usage: a connection can be bound but never used, or bound long ago yet still run daily. find-stale weighs both lastBoundDateTime and lastCredentialUsedDateTime.

NULL recency on old connections: pre-GA connections report NULL even when in use. find-stale skips connections created before --created-after (default 2026-05-01) to avoid false positives — lowering the cutoff re-introduces that risk.

Owner deletion myth: a connection does not fail merely because its owner account is deleted — it fails when the CREDENTIAL used for auth can no longer authenticate (e.g. an OAuth credential tied to the deleted user). A connection using an SPN and shared with others keeps working. Still, single individual ownership is an administration/continuity risk worth fixing.

Visibility scope: for cloud connections you see only the ones you own; a gateway admin sees all connections on that gateway. Run the sweep with the identity that owns/administers the connections you want to govern.
find-single-owner issues one roleAssignments read per connection (there is no bulk API); it skips connections whose role assignments it cannot read rather than aborting the whole sweep.
